intro.title: Welcome to Safi — Ceramics & Atlantic History
intro.p1: Set between Casablanca and Essaouira on Morocco's Atlantic coast, Safi blends centuries of ceramic craftsmanship with Portuguese coastal fortifications, a lively medina and one of the country's major sardine and fishing ports.
intro.p2: Most landmarks sit relatively close together: start on the Potters' Quarter (Colline des Potiers) and the National Ceramics Museum, walk down through the medina and souks toward the Sea Castle (Dar El Bahr) and Kechla, then head to the port or nearby beaches and Cap Safi.

potters_quarter.title: Potters' Quarter (Colline des Potiers)
potters_quarter.p1: Rising above the city, the Potters' Quarter is the beating heart of Safi's craft identity. Dozens of family workshops shape local clay on the wheel, dry pieces in the sun, paint traditional motifs and fire them in kilns.
potters_quarter.p2: Walk through the lanes with time to watch artisans at work and compare glaze patterns directly in the studios and showrooms.
potters_quarter.tip: Visit in the morning when workshops are active; check shipping or packing if buying large pieces.

ceramics_museum.title: National Ceramics Museum
ceramics_museum.p1: Located near the potters' hill, the museum provides helpful context on Safi's pottery traditions, glazes and regional Moroccan ceramic styles before you browse the surrounding workshops.
ceramics_museum.p2: It is compact and easy to pair with a stroll through the adjacent craft lanes.
ceramics_museum.tip: Combine with the Potters' Quarter in the same morning circuit.

sea_castle.title: Sea Castle (Dar El Bahr)
sea_castle.p1: Built along the rocky shore during the Portuguese presence in the 16th century, Dar El Bahr stands right above the Atlantic swells and offers broad views over the coast and harbour entrance.
sea_castle.p2: Its stone ramparts and ocean backdrop make it one of Safi's most atmospheric stops for photography and a short coastal walk.
sea_castle.tip: Watch your footing near wet rocks and windy edges along the sea wall.

kechla.title: Kechla Fortress & Ramparts
kechla.p1: Overlooking the old quarters, the Kechla citadel and historic ramparts reflect Safi's strategic coastal role across centuries of trade and fortification.
kechla.p2: Walk around the outer walls to connect the medina with views over the rooftops and Atlantic horizon.
kechla.tip: Late afternoon light gives strong relief to the old stone walls.

medina.title: Medina & Souks
medina.p1: Safi's medina feels grounded and everyday rather than purely touristic. Winding lanes connect bakeries, spice stalls, small craftsmen and shaded passages.
medina.p2: Take an unhurried walk through the souks to sample local snacks, pick up ceramics or head down toward the seafront.
medina.tip: Go earlier in the day for bustling market stalls and calmer foot traffic.

port.title: Fishing Port & Sardine Harbour
port.p1: Safi's fishing port is a busy working harbour long known for sardine fishing and seafood activity along the Atlantic coast.
port.p2: Mending nets, moored boats and fresh catch create a lively maritime scene, especially when vessels come in.
port.tip: Stay clear of active quays and cranes, and ask before taking close portraits of fishermen.

great_mosque.title: Great Mosque (Grande Mosquée)
great_mosque.p1: Anchoring the historic centre, the Great Mosque and its minaret serve as a familiar reference point while exploring the streets of the old town.
great_mosque.p2: Admire the exterior architecture and surrounding squares as you move between the souks and coastal walls.
great_mosque.tip: Dress modestly around places of worship and avoid blocking entrances at prayer times.

bab_chaaba.title: Bab Chaâba & Old Gates
bab_chaaba.p1: Historic gateways like Bab Chaâba mark the transition between Safi's walled quarters and the wider town, recalling how land routes and coastal defences met.
bab_chaaba.p2: They make natural orientation points when walking between the medina, souks and nearby avenues.
bab_chaaba.tip: Use the historic gates as easy landmarks for a self-guided walking loop.

cap_safi.title: Cap Safi & Atlantic Cliffs
cap_safi.p1: North of the city centre, Cap Safi opens onto rugged Atlantic cliffs, coastal wind and wide ocean horizons away from the dense streets.
cap_safi.p2: It is best reached by car or taxi and rewards visitors looking for coastal scenery and sunset views.
cap_safi.tip: Bring a light windbreaker even on sunny days — Atlantic gusts pick up quickly.

beach_corniche.title: Safi Beach & Corniche
beach_corniche.p1: Safi's seafront promenade and beach area offer a relaxed place to unwind after exploring the medina and workshops, with cafés, ocean air and sunset views.
beach_corniche.p2: Sea conditions and currents vary along the Atlantic coast, so check local conditions before entering the water.
beach_corniche.tip: Ideal for an early-evening walk along the promenade.

lalla_fatna.title: Lalla Fatna Beach
lalla_fatna.p1: Situated north of Safi along the coast, Lalla Fatna is a scenic bay framed by cliffs and hills, popular with local beachgoers and surfers looking for a quieter coastal setting.
lalla_fatna.p2: Because it sits outside the immediate town centre, plan ahead for transport and bring essentials for the day.
lalla_fatna.tip: Great as a half-day coastal escape if you have a car or arranged taxi.

souira_qdima.title: Souira Qdima & Tensift Mouth
souira_qdima.p1: South of Safi where the Tensift River meets the Atlantic, Souira Qdima preserves historic coastal fortifications, quiet dunes and an off-the-beaten-path atmosphere.
souira_qdima.p2: It pairs naturally with a coastal drive heading south toward Essaouira.
souira_qdima.tip: Best visited by car or private driver as an unhurried coastal stop.

timing.title: When to visit
timing.desc: Spring through autumn brings pleasant coastal days; mornings are best for workshops and souks, late afternoons for cliffs and sea views.

q1.question: How long should I spend in Safi?
q1.answer: A full day covers the Potters' Quarter, Ceramics Museum, Sea Castle, Kechla, medina and port; stay one night if you also want Cap Safi or Lalla Fatna at a relaxed pace.

q2.question: What is Safi best known for?
q2.answer: Safi is renowned across Morocco for its traditional ceramics and pottery workshops on the Colline des Potiers, alongside its Portuguese-era coastal fortifications and busy sardine fishing port.

q3.question: Can I visit Safi as a stop between cities?
q3.answer: Yes — Safi works well as a stopover or day trip on road itineraries linking Casablanca or El Jadida with Essaouira or Marrakech.

q4.question: Do I need a car in Safi?
q4.answer: You can explore the medina, Sea Castle, Kechla and potters' hill on foot or by local taxi, while a car makes reaching Cap Safi, Lalla Fatna and Souira Qdima much easier.
